card: Encodes -torpassword as unquoted hex when authenticating to Tor control rather than escaping quoted strings. Currently, passwords containing backslash characters are mangled by Tor's escape parsing and fail authentication. The Tor Control specification explicitly permits hex encoding to bypass string-escaping issues, and this change adds functional test coverage for passwords containing quotes and backslashes.
changed_since_previous: None; the patch matches the earlier description.
evidence: PR description: 'The Tor password was sent as a QuotedString with only double quotes escaped; as Tor interprets backslash escapes inside it, any password containing a backslash was mangled (or left the string unterminated).'
PR description: 'The Tor Control spec deliberately allows the token to be sent as unquoted hex "to avoid escaping issues", as the SAFECOOKIE response already is.'
problem: Tor control passwords containing backslashes fail to authenticate or get mangled. Bitcoin Core previously sent the password as a QuotedString and only escaped double-quote characters, causing Tor's control port parser to misinterpret backslash sequences or report unterminated strings.

risk.why: If hex-encoded authentication is rejected by older or non-standard Tor daemons, nodes configured with -torpassword would fail to authenticate and set up onion services.

summary: Sends the -torpassword argument as a hex-encoded string during Tor control port authentication instead of as an escaped QuotedString. It also adds a functional test verifying that passwords containing backslashes and quotes authenticate successfully against a mock Tor control server.
